meta.storyTitle: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts inline webview script (updatePickers/renderProvPane/renderModelPane/rlabel/pickModel/rb.onclick/gb.onclick) + its host-side call sites in the same file; tests in vscode-plugin/src/chat/__tests__/chat-panel.test.ts

summary.prose: Stop the insrc VS Code chat panel's run-config provider/model popup from flickering while open. Webview-side change-gating in chat-panel.ts: an open popup is rebuilt only when the provider/model/effort or catalog data it shows actually changed; opening the popup no longer forces a catalog refresh when the catalog is already ready; picking a different provider (which starts a new chat) closes the popup instead of leaving it open to be rebuilt by the host echo. Regression tests in chat-panel.test.ts prove each gate.

alternativesConsidered.name: Change-gated re-render in the webview (minimal)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Remember the last-rendered run-config (provider/model/effort) and catalog (revision+status); skip pane rebuilds and label rewrites when an echo carries identical values; skip requestCatalog() on open when the catalog is ready; closePops() on a different-provider pick.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add two small pieces of client state in the chat-panel.ts inline script (lastRunKey, lastCatalogKey). updatePickers()/rlabel() compare before touching the DOM; rb.onclick/gb.onclick only call requestCatalog() when catalogStatus is not ready; pickModel and the provider item onclick call closePops() in the different-provider branch exactly like the same-provider branch. Host side (postRunConfig/publishCatalog/refreshRunCatalog) unchanged.
pros: Smallest change that fully stops the flicker: no message ever rebuilds an open popup unless the shown data changed
No host-side behavior change, so no risk to other message consumers
All edits stay inside the existing inline webview script + existing handlers in chat-panel.ts
cons: Host still posts duplicate echoes (harmless — webview ignores them)
Two extra pieces of client state to keep in sync

alternativesConsidered.name: Host-side echo dedupe
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Make the host omit run-config/run-catalog posts when the values are identical to what was last posted (postRunConfig/publishCatalog compare-and-skip).
alternativesConsidered.approach: In chat-panel.ts host side, keep lastPostedRunConfig/lastPostedCatalog and skip post() when unchanged; webview untouched.
cons: Does not fix the webview-side fragility: any future message that calls updatePickers still rebuilds an open popup
Changes host post behavior shared by other flows (postRunConfig is also called from submitTurn/new-chat refusals), wider blast radius than needed
Does not address the missing closePops() on new-chat provider picks
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Does not fix the webview-side rebuild or the open-popup-after-new-chat-pick case; changes shared host post behavior.

alternativesConsidered.name: Keyed DOM reconciliation of the popup panes
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Rebuild panes via keyed diffing (reuse/move existing .item nodes) so hover and scroll survive any re-render.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Replace the innerHTML rebuilds in renderProvPane/renderModelPane with a small keyed reconciler over catalog entries.
pros: Perfectly preserves hover/scroll even when data changes
More robust against future re-render triggers
cons: Meaningfully more code inside the CSP-bound inline script for a two-pane menu
Overkill when change-gating (a1) already prevents spurious re-renders entirely
Higher regression risk in the hand-rolled webview script
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Oversized: change-gating (a1) already eliminates spurious re-renders entirely.
